A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StreamDiffusion and retain matching methods and experiments. The complete text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. v1 ends with references; v2's appendices and supplementary figures are available and readable.

before.justification: v1 reports original inference-time comparisons, component ablations, GPU power measurements, and generated-image examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds FID/CLIP results, user-preference studies, and temporal-consistency examples.

M1.justification: v2 Section 3.2 introduces Stream Batch cross-frame attention, using keys and values from past and future frames at different denoising stages. This changes the inference procedure beyond v1's batching of individual frames. R-CFG and SSF retain their underlying procedures.

E1.justification: v2 adds text-to-image quality evaluation on data identified through the InstructPix2Pix citation and human preference evaluation. The principal image-generation domains remain unchanged. Audio and robotic action generation are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates LCM as a direct FID/CLIP comparator and a hard-threshold similarity filter in the user study. v1 used LCM within its pipeline and discussed hard thresholds without reporting these comparisons. Existing AutoPipeline, sequential-denoising, and CFG comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds FID/CLIP evaluation and four human-preference comparisons with reported samples of 486, 144, 45, and 257 users. It also specifies four-step denoising for the cross-frame examples. The existing 100-image timing and 20/1000-frame energy-evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds temporal-consistency comparisons with and without cross-frame attention in Figure 9 and Table 3. Its user studies also examine SSF quality preservation, stochastic versus hard-threshold filtering, and guidance preferences. The original timing ablations are largely retained and replotted.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed specifications, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new user counts and preference percentages describe evaluation samples and outcomes, without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports LCM versus StreamDiffusion FID of 29.69 versus 26.79 and CLIP scores of 24.95 versus 24.99. Table 3 adds preference results, including 90.33% favoring future-frame attention and 75.56% favoring SSF over hard thresholds. Timing Tables 1–2 and the reported power measurements remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds mathematical definitions of the staggered key/value batches and their cross-frame attention computation. The R-CFG derivation is reorganized around self-consistency but largely preserves the earlier algebra. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v2 adds future-frame conditioning and improved temporal consistency as central contributions. Its introduction also reframes Stream Batch as a broader Stream Denoising framework claiming continuous, unbounded video, audio, and robotic-action generation. The original headline speed and power claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains latency and synchronization advantages over naive Waiting and Batching, and how future-frame context can accommodate abrupt input changes. It adds interpretations of the quality and preference results. Existing qualifications concerning R-CFG's image-to-image scope, contrast instability, and TensorRT dimension constraints remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies four denoising steps for the new cross-frame examples. Appendix A retains most implementation details but omits v1's explicit statement about reusing each step's sampled noise across frames; this does not establish a changed cache policy. Hardware, acceleration tools, and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion is substantially expanded and reorganized, including a dedicated CFG discussion, SDEdit-specific positioning, and an explicit contrast with Parallel Sampling's latency objective. New references cover rectified flow, diffusion policies, perception, and other diffusion developments; several earlier acceleration references disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and R-CFG explanation undergo substantial rewriting. Engineering sections move into Appendix A, text-to-image discussion moves into Appendix B, and the experiment narrative is reorganized around efficiency and quality. Terminology changes from RCFG to R-CFG.

P2.justification: The pipeline, batching, guidance, and queue diagrams are redrawn. The component timing table becomes a bar chart, while a user-study table and temporal-consistency figure are added; several existing figures move to the appendix. Figure 1 shortens the earlier image grid and introduces an unexplained StreamDiT-4B caption.

improvement.justification: The explicit cross-frame mechanism and new quantitative and human evaluations strengthen evidence about visual quality and temporal consistency, which v1 supported chiefly through examples. The gains are limited by sparse benchmark and user-study protocols, untested audio/robotics generalizations, and the unexplained StreamDiT-4B teaser caption.
